# requireNonFunctionLike

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not callable.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonFunctionLike() — Returns the value after checking that it is not callable. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonFunctionLike<T>( // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-function-type value: T | Function, message: string = "Expected a non-function value." ): T;
```

The cheap test — `typeof value === "function"` — which is what you want before calling something. `isFunction` is the stricter reading of the same question.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                   | Type            | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                     | `T \| Function` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-function value."` | `string`        | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with callable excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition              |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is callable. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonFunctionLike(null); // => null
requireNonFunctionLike({}); // => {}
requireNonFunctionLike(function () {}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonFunctionLike(Math.max); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
